questions.prompt: Which gas makes up about 78% of clean air?
questions.why: Air mainly contains nitrogen (78%).
questions.quote: Air is a mixture of gases. It contains nitrogen (78%), oxygen (21%), carbon dioxide (0.04%), noble gases (about 0.9%), water vapour and other gases.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up about 21% of air?
questions.why: Air contains oxygen (21%).
questions.quote: Air is a mixture of gases. It contains nitrogen (78%), oxygen (21%), carbon dioxide (0.04%), noble gases (about 0.9%), water vapour and other gases.

questions.prompt: What percentage of air is carbon dioxide?
questions.why: Carbon dioxide makes up 0.04% of air.
questions.quote: carbon dioxide (0.04%)

questions.prompt: What happens to a glowing splint in oxygen?
questions.why: Oxygen relights a glowing splint.
questions.quote: It relights a glowing splint.

questions.prompt: What does carbon dioxide turn lime water into?
questions.why: Carbon dioxide turns lime water from colourless to milky.
questions.quote: It turns lime water from colourless to milky.

questions.prompt: What does water do to dry cobalt chloride paper?
questions.why: Water turns dry cobalt chloride paper from blue to pink.
questions.quote: It turns dry cobalt chloride paper from blue to pink.

questions.prompt: How is nitrogen best described?
questions.why: Nitrogen is unreactive.
questions.quote: Nitrogen is unreactive.

questions.prompt: Which property of oxygen makes it useful for welding metals?
questions.why: Oxygen supports burning, giving a very hot flame for cutting and welding metals.
questions.quote: Oxygen supports burning.

questions.prompt: At what temperature does dry ice change directly to gas?
questions.why: Dry ice changes from solid to gas directly at –78 °C.
questions.quote: It changes to gas directly at –78 °C (i.e. without going through the liquid state).

questions.prompt: Which best describes a mixture?
questions.why: A mixture forms when substances mix without making a new substance.
questions.quote: A mixture is formed when two or more substances mix with each other without the formation of a new substance.

questions.prompt: What percentage of clean air is noble gases?
questions.why: Noble gases make up about 0.9% of air.
questions.quote: noble gases (about 0.9%)

questions.prompt: What is nitrogen's boiling point?
questions.why: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of –196 °C.
questions.quote: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point (–196 °C).

questions.prompt: Which gas does not support burning?
questions.why: Carbon dioxide does not support burning.
questions.quote: Carbon dioxide does not support burning.

questions.prompt: Why do helium-filled balloons float in air?
options: Helium is less dense than air
questions.why: Helium is less dense than air, so helium balloons float.
questions.quote: As helium is less dense than air, helium-filled balloons float in air.

questions.prompt: Which gases are used to fill neon signs?
questions.why: Argon and neon are used to fill neon signs.
questions.quote: Argon and neon are used to fill neon signs.

questions.prompt: Why is nitrogen used in food packets?
options: Replace air to keep food longer
To make the food taste sweeter
questions.why: Nitrogen replaces air in food packets to prevent food from reacting with oxygen.
questions.quote: Nitrogen is used to replace the air in food packets.

questions.prompt: What can liquid nitrogen be used for?
options: Storage of living cells or tissues
questions.why: Liquid nitrogen can be used in the storage of living cells or tissues.
questions.quote: Liquid nitrogen can be used in the storage of living cells or tissues (e.g. cord blood).

questions.prompt: What gas is contained in some fire extinguishers?
questions.why: Some fire extinguishers contain carbon dioxide.
questions.quote: Some fire extinguishers contain carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Why does carbon dioxide from a fire extinguisher put out a fire?
options: It turns the fire into fog
questions.why: Carbon dioxide sinks and displaces the air around the fire, cutting off oxygen supply.
questions.quote: Carbon dioxide released from the fire extinguisher sinks and displaces the air surrounding the fire. This cuts off the oxygen supply and helps put out the fire.

questions.prompt: What is liquid nitrogen used for in commercial freezing systems?
questions.why: Liquid nitrogen is used to freeze foods like fruits rapidly.
questions.quote: Liquid nitrogen is used in commercial freezing systems to freeze foods like fruits rapidly.
